aiItems.content:
What is 3 piece wall art?

3 piece wall art is a coordinated set of three individual art prints designed to be displayed together as a group, creating a unified visual statement on your wall. Each print in the set shares a common colour palette, theme, or style so they look intentional and cohesive side by side. You can hang them in a straight horizontal row, a staggered arrangement, or even spread across a larger wall for a gallery effect. They're a brilliant choice when you want to fill a wide space — like above a fireplace or along a hallway — without the guesswork of mixing different prints yourself. Because the hard work of matching is already done, a set of 3 is one of the easiest ways to create a polished, decorator-level look in any room.

How to Hang 3 Piece Wall Art Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure to find the width of your chimney breast or the wall space above the fireplace. Aim for your three prints together to span roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of that width — wide enough to feel balanced, but with breathing room on either side.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of the wall lightly with a pencil. Your middle print should be centred on this point. This keeps the whole arrangement visually anchored and symmetrical above the mantel.

3. Set your hanging height: The bottom edge of your prints should sit roughly 15–20 cm above the mantel shelf. This keeps them connected to the fireplace as a feature rather than floating too high up the wall.

4. Space the prints evenly: Leave a consistent gap between each print — 4–6 cm is a good rule of thumb for a neat, intentional look. Use a spirit level to make sure all three are perfectly aligned horizontally before you commit to the fixings.

5. Step back and check: Before making any permanent marks, hold the prints up against the wall (or use paper templates cut to size) and step back to see how the arrangement looks at a distance. Adjust the height or spacing if anything feels off — it's much easier now than after the nails are in.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Your Choices

Unframed Print — The print only, shipped flat and ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want to match a very specific frame style or colour. Available in Luster or Museum quality art paper.

Framed Print — Arrives fully assembled and ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping, no measuring, no fuss. The most convenient option if you want the set on the wall as quickly as possible. Available in Luster or Museum quality art paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed on canvas and stretched around a wooden frame — no glass, no mount, just the art itself with a tactile, painted feel. Arrives ready to hang and suits the oil-painting aesthetic of this bohemian book set particularly well. Available in multiple sizes.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish with a gentle sheen that makes warm earthy tones and greens pop. Works beautifully in naturally lit rooms such as a study or sitting room above the fireplace.

Museum Quality Paper — A smooth, flat matte finish with a gallery feel. Ideal for rooms with more atmospheric, lower lighting, or for anyone who wants the art to look as close to an original painting as possible.

What is canvas 3 piece wall art?

Canvas 3 piece wall art is a set of three coordinating art prints designed to be displayed together as a group, creating a cohesive and visually balanced arrangement on your wall. Each print in the set shares a common theme, colour palette or style so that, hung side by side, they look like one considered, intentional display rather than three random pieces. The term 'canvas' is used broadly — the set can come as wrapped canvas prints, framed prints or unframed prints on art paper, depending on the finish you prefer. They are particularly popular for hallways, living rooms, study rooms and reading nooks because a set of three fills a wall with personality in a way a single print simply cannot. Choosing a set also takes the guesswork out of curating a gallery wall yourself — the hard work of matching colours and subjects is already done for you.

How to Hang Canvas 3 Piece Wall Art in a Hallway or Reading Nook

1. Measure your wall first: Note the full width of the wall you want to use. Aim for the combined width of all three prints plus the gaps between them to fill roughly two-thirds of that space — this gives the set visual weight without overwhelming the room.

2. Mark your centre point: Find the centre of the wall and use a pencil mark or a strip of painter's tape to mark it. Your middle print should sit centred on this point, making the whole arrangement balanced and symmetrical.

3. Decide on your gaps: A gap of 5–8 cm between each print is the sweet spot for a neat, gallery-style look. Use strips of card cut to that width as spacers while you mark your hanging points — it keeps everything even without lots of measuring.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of the middle print should sit at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is the standard eye-level guideline that works for most people and most rooms. In a hallway with lower ceilings, you can drop this slightly.

5. Check alignment with a spirit level: Before you commit to the final nails or fixings, hold each print up in position and use a small spirit level or a level app on your phone to make sure all three are perfectly straight and level with each other. This is the step most people skip — and it really does make a difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Format: Canvas 3 Piece Wall Art Options Compared

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A versatile, cost-effective option that lets you choose your own frame. Luster paper gives a subtle sheen that makes colours pop and handles light well — great for everyday display in hallways or study rooms.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The premium paper choice for collectors and those who want the sharpest, most gallery-accurate colour reproduction. A heavier, fine-art finish that looks stunning when framed and is built to last for years.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum Quality) — Arrives ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping needed. The frame and print are matched and fitted for you, which is ideal if you want a clean, polished result without the hassle of sourcing a frame separately. Available in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a textured, painterly feel that suits the oil-painting style of this bohemian books set particularly well. No frame needed — the canvas wraps around the edges and hangs as-is. A great choice if you want something that feels more like original artwork on your wall.

aiItems.content:
What is artwork for the living room?

Artwork for the living room refers to any wall art print, canvas or framed image chosen specifically to suit a living space — enhancing its personality, colour scheme and atmosphere. The best living room art reflects the people who live there, whether that's bold abstract colour, calming botanicals or, as with this bohemian books set, a warm and personal still-life scene that celebrates everyday pleasures like reading and a good cup of tea. Living room wall art typically comes as single prints, pairs or sets — a set of three, like this one, is particularly popular because it fills a wall with a cohesive story without requiring you to mix and match different pieces yourself. Choosing art for the living room is really about finding something that feels right for the space and genuinely right for you.

How to Hang and Style Artwork for the Living Room: A Simple Step-by-Step

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall that gets good natural or artificial light and where the prints will be at eye level when you're seated — above a sofa, beside a reading chair or over a console table are all great spots for this set.

2. Measure your space: Hold the three prints up against the wall (or use paper cut-outs the same size) to check they'll fill roughly two-thirds of the wall width. Mark the centre point of your display with a light pencil dot.

3. Map out the layout: Lay the three prints on the floor in front of the wall to plan your spacing. A gap of 5–8 cm between each print looks balanced — close enough to read as a set, with enough breathing room to appreciate each one individually.

4. Hang the centre print first: Fix the middle print at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print is the standard guide). Use a spirit level to make sure it's straight.

5. Add the outer prints: Working outwards from the centre, hang the left and right prints at exactly the same height, maintaining your chosen gap. Step back and check the alignment — adjust as needed before any marks become permanent.

6. Style around them: These prints work beautifully with warm-toned accessories — think natural wood, wicker baskets, a cosy throw or a small stack of real books on a shelf below. Let the art lead the room's colour story.

Which Option Is Right for You? Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas

Finish — Unframed print: print only, you choose and source your own frame. Framed print: arrives complete and ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: artwork printed and stretched over a wooden frame, no additional framing needed.

Effort to hang — Unframed print: requires your own frame and fitting. Framed print: ready to hang straight out of the box. Wrapped canvas: ready to hang straight out of the box.

Paper / material choice — Unframed print: available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: canvas material — no paper option.

Look and feel — Unframed print: flexible — suits any frame style you choose. Framed print: clean, polished, gallery-ready finish. Wrapped canvas: painterly, textured, gallery-wrap appearance with no frame required.

Best for — Unframed print: those who already have frames or want full control over the framing style. Framed print: anyone who wants a fuss-free, complete result. Wrapped canvas: those who love a natural, painted-art aesthetic on the wall.

aiItems.content:
What is 3 piece wall art framed?

A 3 piece wall art framed set is a group of three coordinating art prints designed to be displayed together as a single arrangement on your wall. Each print shares a common colour palette, theme or style so that the trio looks cohesive and considered rather than random. You can hang them in a horizontal row, a vertical column, or even in a stepped arrangement depending on your wall space. Framed sets are especially popular above a fireplace, sofa or bed because they fill a wide wall beautifully while keeping things visually balanced and unified.

How to Hang 3 Piece Wall Art Framed Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall: Start by measuring the width of your chimney breast or the wall space above your fireplace. As a guide, aim for the full spread of all three prints to cover roughly two thirds of that width — this keeps things balanced and stops the set looking too small or too crowded.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of the wall and mark it lightly with a pencil. The middle print should sit centred on this point, with the two flanking prints placed at an even distance on either side — a gap of around 5 to 8 cm between each print looks neat and intentional.

3. Set your hanging height: The centre of the middle print should sit roughly at eye level, or around 15 to 20 cm above the mantelpiece shelf — whichever feels more balanced in your room. Hold the prints up against the wall before committing to make sure you're happy with the height.

4. Use a spirit level: Before you hammer any nails, use a spirit level or a free smartphone app to make sure all three prints are perfectly aligned horizontally. Even a small tilt can make the whole arrangement look off, so it's worth taking an extra minute here.

5. Step back and adjust: Once hung, step back and look at the set from across the room — this is the view most people will have. Small tweaks to spacing or height at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas — Which Option is Right for You?

Ready to hang straight away — Framed print: Yes, arrives ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: Yes, arrives ready to hang. Unframed print: No — you source and fit your own frame or mount.

Frame included — Framed print: Yes. Wrapped canvas: No frame; the print wraps around a deep wooden stretcher bar. Unframed print: No.

Best for a gallery or painted look — Framed print: Gallery look with a defined border. Wrapped canvas: Painterly, frameless feel — great for a bohemian or relaxed style. Unframed print: Flexible — style it however you like.

Paper / surface choice — Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: Canvas wrap (no paper option).

Ideal if you — Framed print: Want a neat, finished look with no extra effort. Wrapped canvas: Love a more relaxed, contemporary feel. Unframed print: Already have a favourite frame or prefer to customise the presentation yourself.

aiItems.content:
What is framed 3 piece wall art?

Framed 3 piece wall art is a coordinated set of three individual art prints designed to be displayed together as one cohesive arrangement on your wall. Each print in the set shares the same colour palette, style or theme so that when hung side by side — or in another arrangement that suits your space — they look intentional and complete. Unlike buying individual prints separately, a set of 3 gives you an instant, ready-to-style grouping with no guesswork about whether pieces will complement each other. At AboutWallArt, our sets are available as unframed prints, framed prints or wrapped canvases in a range of sizes, so you can tailor the look entirely to your home.

How to Hang Framed 3 Piece Wall Art in a Hallway or Study

1. Measure your wall first: Use a tape measure to find the width of your wall space. Aim for the combined width of all three prints (plus the gaps between them) to fill around two thirds of the available width — this gives a balanced, considered look rather than feeling either too cramped or too sparse.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall space and mark it lightly with a pencil. Hang the middle print first, centred on that mark at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print). This gives you a fixed anchor to work outward from.

3. Space the outer prints evenly: Measure an even gap of 5–8 cm from the edge of the centre print and position the left and right prints at exactly the same height. Use a spirit level to keep all three aligned horizontally — even a small tilt is noticeable once the prints are up.

4. Step back and adjust: Before you commit to the final fixings, hold or lightly tack each print in place and step back to check the overall look. In a hallway, natural light changes through the day, so check at different times if you can — the moody grey tones in this set can shift beautifully depending on the light.

Choosing Your Format: Unframed Print, Framed Print or Wrapped Canvas

Unframed Print — The print only, on your choice of Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Great if you already have frames you love or want to choose your own framing to match your existing décor. You'll need to source and fit your own frames.

Framed Print — Your chosen print on Luster or Museum quality paper, supplied ready to hang — no extra trips to find a frame that fits. A brilliant time-saver and the most popular choice for hallways where you want a polished, finished look straight away.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, arriving ready to hang. No paper, no glass — just a clean, contemporary look with real texture and depth. Ideal if you prefer a more relaxed, bohemian feel without the formality of a framed print.

Paper finish (prints only) — Luster art paper has a gentle semi-sheen that makes colours look vivid and rich. Museum quality paper is a premium matt finish with exceptional colour accuracy and fine detail — perfect for viewing up close in a reading nook or study.

aiItems.content:
What is a canvas painting for living room?

A canvas painting for living room is a decorative art print or wrapped canvas designed to add colour, personality and warmth to your main living space. They come in a wide range of styles — from abstract and botanical to still-life and bohemian — and are available as single pieces or coordinating sets. Sets of three are particularly popular because they create an instant gallery-wall effect without the guesswork of mixing and matching individual pieces. Whether printed on art paper with a frame or stretched over a canvas wrap, they are one of the quickest and most effective ways to pull a room together and make it feel truly like home.

How to Hang a Canvas Painting for Living Room: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold a piece of tape or use painter's tape on the wall to mark out the rough footprint of all three prints together, including the gaps between them. Step back and check you are happy with the placement before making any holes.

2. Find the right height: The centre of your set should sit roughly at eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor is the standard guide for most living rooms. If hanging above a sofa or console, leave about 20–25 cm of space between the top of the furniture and the bottom of the prints.

3. Space the prints evenly: For a clean, gallery look, keep the gap between each of the three prints consistent — 5 to 8 cm is usually ideal. Use a spirit level or a free levelling app on your phone to keep everything straight.

4. Mark and hang: Lightly mark each hanging point in pencil, fix your hooks or picture nails, and hang the prints one at a time, checking the level as you go. Framed and canvas-wrapped options come ready to hang, so no extra hardware is needed.

5. Stand back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back across the room and check the spacing and level with fresh eyes. Small adjustments make a big difference to the finished look.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Our Canvas Painting for Living Room Formats

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A versatile option if you already have frames at home or prefer to choose your own. Luster paper gives a soft sheen that enhances the depth of dark, moody artwork like this set. Post flat in protective packaging.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — A matte, fine-art finish that reduces glare — ideal if your living room receives strong natural or artificial light. Crisp, gallery-standard results with no shine.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum Quality) — Arrives completely ready to hang straight out of the packaging — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A great all-in-one solution if you want a polished, finished look immediately.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a solid frame, giving a relaxed, studio-art feel. No frame or glass required — just hang and enjoy. Available in its own range of sizes and suits bohemian or casual-eclectic interiors especially well.
